subsystems.name: Renewable power and water treatment
subsystems.role: supplies cheap electricity and the ultrapure water an electrolyser needs.

subsystems.name: Electrolyser bank
subsystems.role: splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using renewable electricity.

subsystems.name: Air separation unit
subsystems.role: extracts nitrogen from the air — roughly four-fifths of the atmosphere.

subsystems.name: Synthesis loop
subsystems.role: combines hydrogen and nitrogen into ammonia over a catalyst.

subsystems.name: Storage and export
subsystems.role: holds a toxic, corrosive liquid fuel until it is used or shipped.
parts: flare and scrubber for safe venting

subsystems.name: End use or reconversion
subsystems.role: turns ammonia back into fertiliser, fuel or electricity.
parts: cracking catalyst and furnace for hydrogen

buildSteps.title: Generate renewable hydrogen
buildSteps.detail: Electrolysers run on wind or solar power, splitting purified water into hydrogen and oxygen. Output is intermittent, so the plant needs storage or flexible operation.

buildSteps.title: Separate nitrogen from air
buildSteps.detail: A cryogenic air separation unit cools air until it liquefies, then distils nitrogen from oxygen — an energy-hungry step that is often the second-largest load on site.

buildSteps.title: Compress the feed gas
buildSteps.detail: Hydrogen and nitrogen are mixed in roughly a three-to-one ratio and compressed to the pressure the synthesis loop needs, around 100–200 bar.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise ammonia
buildSteps.detail: The hot, high-pressure gas passes over an iron catalyst at several hundred degrees Celsius; some of it combines into ammonia, which is chilled out as liquid and the unreacted gas is recycled.

buildSteps.title: Store and handle safely
buildSteps.detail: Ammonia is kept as a refrigerated liquid near −33 °C or under pressure. Because it is toxic and attacks copper alloys, tanks, seals and pipework are specified for it.

buildSteps.title: Ship or use directly
buildSteps.detail: Most goes to fertiliser plants; some is burned in engines or turbines, or cracked back into hydrogen at 500–600 °C. Reconversion to electricity returns well under half the energy put in.

buildSteps.title: Prove it at scale
buildSteps.detail: Today's green plants have tens of megawatts of electrolysis. Scaling to match a conventional world-scale ammonia train means hundreds of megawatts of electrolysis running reliably.

prerequisites.why: power is the dominant cost of green hydrogen, and hydrogen dominates the cost of green ammonia.
modules of tens of megawatts exist and are being scaled up, but fleets of hundreds of megawatts are unproven.
the century-old industrial route is well understood; the innovation is feeding it renewable hydrogen instead of gas-derived hydrogen.
turning ammonia back into hydrogen at useful rates is demonstrated but energy-intensive and not deployed at scale.
ammonia ignites poorly and needs a pilot fuel; engines and bunkering rules are only now entering service.

pathway.milestone: green ammonia demonstration plants with tens of megawatts of electrolysis, mostly making fertiliser
pathway.unlocks: a working supply chain: renewable power to electrolyser to synthesis to a shipped product.

pathway.milestone: hundreds-of-megawatts plants co-located with solar or wind in high-resource regions
pathway.unlocks: green ammonia at prices that start to compete where gas is expensive or carbon is priced.

pathway.milestone: ammonia dual-fuel ships and co-firing in power plants
pathway.unlocks: a second, very large market that pulls investment into production and bunkering infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: import corridors that ship ammonia from sunny and windy coasts to industrial centres, cracking some of it back to hydrogen
pathway.unlocks: long-duration energy storage and hydrogen supply for regions that cannot make their own.
